The **Bengal cat** is a breed of hybrid "Hybrid (biology)") cat created from crossbreeding an Asian leopard cat to domestic cats (*Prionailurus bengalensis* × *Felis catus*), especially the spotted tabby Egyptian Mau. Bengals have varying appearances. The breed is selectively bred and pedigree registered with most of the major cat registries. The breed's name derives from that of the Asian leopard cat (*Prionailurus bengalensis*), from which the Bengal cat was originally hybridised. The earliest mention of an Asian leopard cat × domestic cat hybrid was in 1889, when Harrison Weir wrote of them in *Our Cats and All About Them*. The Cat Fanciers' Association (CFA) accepted the Bengal in CFA's "Miscellaneous" in 2016, under the restrictions that "it must be F6 or later (6 generations removed from the Asian leopard cat or non-Bengal domestic cat ancestors)".
